open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: If that record cannot be stored, the kernel process stops all the same, and recovery executes the element again, as it does every function element without a concluded record.
open_points.question: Does this recovery rule apply only to function elements of runs, or also to sandbox executions performed by admission and explicit try operations, which have TrialExecutions rather than run elements?
options: Only a run's function element is re-executed during start-up recovery; an interrupted admission is rerun only on a later submission, and an interrupted explicit try is never recovered automatically.
Every sandbox execution whose concluding record could not be stored is re-executed during start-up recovery, including admission and explicit-try executions.
Run elements are recovered at start-up; admission executions are rerun on the next submission; explicit-try executions require another explicit try.
open_points.default_guess: Only run function elements are re-executed during start-up recovery; admission restarts on the next submission and explicit tries are not recovered automatically.

witness.initial: An existing implementation and trial case exist, and no run is active.
events: An agent calls try_implementation for that case.
The sandbox finishes with unconfirmed cleanup.
The store fails to write the TrialExecution, and the kernel stops.
The host restarts the kernel without another try request.
outcomes: Reading the changed A03 sentence over every function execution, start-up recovery executes the implementation again and may write a TrialExecution.
Following the defined start-up sequence, only in-flight effects and runs are recovered; the explicit try is not executed again and no TrialExecution appears.
witness.observer: The owner or agent inspecting trial executions after restart
